entries.name: Seated Cable Shoulder Press
techniqueCitations: Haff, G. G., & Triplett, N. T. (Eds.). (2016). Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (4th ed.). Human Kinetics, pp. 377-380.
McGill, S. M., et al. (2019). Effects of seated and standing Barbell Back Squats on trunk and shoulder biomechanics. Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research, 33(8), 2362-2371.
entries.reason: Redrawn on 9 October 2026 at the owner's request, because the earlier drawing was against this text: the trunk leaned forward. Source-bound draft, drawn from a 3D model turned 65 degrees: sitting tall on a flat bench between two low pulleys with a handle in each hand, upper arms out to the sides and forearms upright; the handles are pressed up and together overhead until the arms are straight, a pause, and a slower lowering. Each cable only lengthens on the way up. The trunk and legs do not move. With the forearms upright over elbows bent to about a right angle, the hands start a little above the shoulders.
entries.summary: Sitting tall between two low cables with the handles by the shoulders and the upper arms out to the sides, press them up and together overhead, pause, then lower slowly.

frames.caption: Sit tall holding a cable handle in each hand at shoulder height, upper arms out to the sides and elbows bent to about a right angle.
Press the handles up and together overhead until the arms are straight.
Lower them slowly to shoulder height, keeping tension on the cables.

entries.name: Seated Dumbbell Press
techniqueCitations: Haff, G. G., & Triplett, N. T. (Eds.). (2016). Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (4th ed.). Human Kinetics, pp. 377-380.
McGill, S. M., et al. (2019). Effects of seated and standing Barbell Back Squats on trunk and shoulder biomechanics. Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research, 33(8), 2362-2371.
entries.reason: Redrawn on 9 October 2026 at the owner's request, because the earlier drawing was against this text: no back support was drawn and the trunk leaned forward. Source-bound draft, drawn from a 3D model turned 60 degrees so both the back support and the path of the arms show: sitting back against a bench with a back support, a dumbbell at each shoulder with the palms forward; the dumbbells are pressed overhead until they meet at the top, a pause, and a slower lowering to the shoulders. The forearms stay upright and the trunk stays on the bench. Not drawn: cleaning the dumbbells up from the thighs.
entries.summary: Sitting back against a bench with a back support, press the dumbbells from the shoulders until they meet overhead, pause, then lower under control with the back on the bench.

frames.caption: Sit on a bench with a back support, a dumbbell in each hand cleaned from the thighs to shoulder height, palms turned to face forward.
Brace, then press both dumbbells overhead until they meet at the top.
Pause. Stack the wrists over the elbows.
Lower to the shoulders under control.
Keep the back on the bench. When the back arches off it, reduce the load.

entries.name: Kettlebell Seated Press
entries.reason: Source-bound draft, drawn from a 3D model turned 72 degrees so both wide-straddled legs on the floor, the kettlebell resting on the forearm in the rack, and the up-and-out press path all read clearly at card size: sitting directly on the floor with no bench and the legs spread wide for a stable base, pressing one kettlebell up and out from the shoulder rack until the elbow locks overhead, and returning to the rack under control.
entries.summary: Sitting on the floor with the legs spread wide and one kettlebell resting on the forearm at the shoulder, press up and out until the arm locks out overhead, then return to the rack position under control.

frames.caption: Sit on the floor with the legs spread comfortably wide for a stable base, and clean one kettlebell to the shoulder so the bell rests on the forearm.
Press up and out until the arm locks out overhead.
Keep the legs wide and settled, and finish with the elbow locked overhead.
Return to the shoulder under control.
Lower back to the rack position with intent while the wide legs stay settled on the floor.
